c4isr_products.name: Lattice OS / Lattice command and control
c4isr_products.description: AI-enabled C2 and sensor-fusion software that ingests feeds from radars, EO/IR, EW, drones and third-party systems, maintains a track/entity picture, and lets operators task effectors and autonomous systems. Selected by the Army as the common data layer baseline for NGC2 (June 2026), as fire-control platform for IBCS-M counter-UAS (Nov 2025), and as JIATF-401 enterprise counter-UAS C2 (Mar 2026).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: sensor tracks, video, radio/vehicle telemetry, third-party app data. Process: fusion/correlation, computer vision classification, kill-chain automation, tasking. Output: common operational picture, alerts, fire-control recommendations, tasks to effectors/drones. Users: air defense operators, division/brigade staffs (4th ID), SOF operators, CBP agents.

c4isr_products.name: Lattice Mesh
c4isr_products.description: Edge-to-cloud data mesh (publish/subscribe data distribution over DDIL networks) underpinning the NGC2 prototype; company says it expanded to 65+ tactical edge nodes (Mar 2026) and 160+ tactical edge computers / 2,500+ end-user devices / 40 apps at Ivy Mass (May 2026). Also used in CDAO Edge Data Mesh (DefenseNews 2025-07-21).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: entity/task/object data from any Lattice-integrated node. Process: replication, multi-path routing across tactical radios/SATCOM/wired, offline-first sync. Output: shared data layer consumed by third-party apps (Palantir, Rune TyrOS, Shift5, LMI SHEPRD, Onebrief). Users: Army division/brigade/battalion staffs and vehicle crews.

c4isr_products.name: Lattice for Mission Autonomy
c4isr_products.description: Hardware-agnostic platform for tasking teams of heterogeneous uncrewed systems; USSOCOM Mission Autonomy Systems Integration Partner ($86M, 3 years, Mar 2025). Optional integration with Barracuda missiles, Fury CCA, Ghost/Ghost-X drones.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: vehicle control/sensor/payload interfaces. Process: mission planning, collaborative autonomy behaviors, V&V infrastructure. Output: coordinated multi-vehicle effects under human supervision. Users: SOF and joint uncrewed-systems operators.

c4isr_products.name: Lattice SDK
c4isr_products.description: Developer SDK with Entities, Tasks, Objects and Video APIs over gRPC and REST; SDKs published in Python, Go, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust and C++ on GitHub; PyPI package anduril-lattice-sdk v5.1.0 released 2026-09-16 (first release 2025-02-25). Access to a Lattice environment is via an 'Anduril representative' (not self-serve).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: third-party sensors, apps, data services. Process: standardized data models (entity/task/object). Output: integrations that publish to and consume from Lattice. Users: partner developers (e.g., Shift5 integrated in ~2 months; Rune 'within hours').

companies.exact_problem_solved: Turning fragmented, stovepiped sensor and C2 data into a single fused, taskable picture that keeps working across denied/degraded networks, and shortening the sensor-to-effector chain (counter-UAS fire control, division fires, SOF autonomy) without waiting on program-of-record integration timelines.

companies.apis_sdks_open_interfaces: FACT: Lattice SDK (developer.anduril.com) exposes Entities, Tasks, Objects and Video APIs over gRPC and REST with standardized data models; official SDKs on GitHub for Python, Go, Java, JavaScript, Rust and C++; sample apps (auto-reconnaissance, AIS integration, entity visualizer). PyPI anduril-lattice-sdk v5.1.0 (2026-09-16), OAuth2 client credentials. Access to environments is through an Anduril representative (not open sign-up). Company claims Lattice is 'open architecture'; independent verification of openness is limited to observed rapid third-party onboarding in NGC2 (Shift5, Rune, LMI, Onebrief).
companies.security_classification_requirements: FACT: NGC2 apps have been deployed at IL6 (Secret) inside the Lattice-hosted ecosystem (LMI SHEPRD claim, May 2026); Anduril said the mesh supported a sensor-to-effector sequence across security domains (Mar 2026). FACT: a leaked Sept 2025 Army memo flagged 'very high risk' cybersecurity issues in the NGC2 prototype (access logging/least privilege); Army called it a monthly risk roll-up. Classified/ITAR work implies U.S.-person and facility-clearance requirements; specifics not public.
companies.allied_international_activity: FACT: Royal Australian Navy Ghost Shark program of record; Anduril Australia factory. FACT (company): Japan expansion with JMSDF Lattice demonstrations. FACT (Tier 3): UK T&E with British Army and RAF; DSEI 2025 demo. REPORTED (Tier 3, LOW-MEDIUM): NATO selected Lattice for next-generation air C2 (Jerusalem Post 2026-07-09) - not verified against NCIA. Israel office being set up (Globes 2026-08/09).
companies.technical_differentiator: A deployed edge-first data mesh plus C2 UI with a real SDK and demonstrated third-party onboarding in weeks, sold under an enterprise vehicle that lets Army units order software and hardware without new competitions. Vertical integration with its own effectors (Roadrunner, Barracuda, Fury) shortens the sensor-to-effector loop for counter-UAS.
companies.suspected_moat: INFERENCE (MEDIUM): contractual/architectural lock-in via the $20B enterprise vehicle and the NGC2 common data baseline (other vendors must integrate to Lattice data models); capital advantage ($5B raise) to fund manufacturing; operational data from live Army/SOF use. HYPOTHESIS: the moat is weaker at the application layer, where the Army explicitly wants many vendors and soldier-built apps on the data layer.
major_competitors: Palantir (partner in NGC2 but competes for the data/ontology layer and Maven C2)
Lockheed Martin team (25th ID NGC2 full-stack lead)
companies.obvious_weaknesses: Cybersecurity findings on NGC2 prototype (Sept 2025 memo); connectivity gaps observed in field testing (Business Insider Jul 2026); reported ~$1.2B projected 2026 operating loss and extreme valuation (LOW confidence figure); heavy dependence on OTA/enterprise vehicles that remain politically exposed; potential conflicts as both platform owner and effector vendor; export/ITAR constraints on allied sales.
companies.evidence_user_adoption: STRONG: entire 4th ID on NGC2 at Ivy Mass (May 2026); JIATF-401 chose Lattice as common C-UAS C2; SOCOM multi-year integration since 2022; CBP long-term use. Adoption numbers are largely company- or Army-stated; independent user surveys not found.
companies.evidence_repeat_procurement: STRONG: sequence of Army awards (NGC2 prototype Jul 2025 -> IBCS-M Nov 2025 -> $20B enterprise vehicle Mar 2026 -> $87M task order Mar 2026 -> NGC2 baseline lead Jun 2026 -> TITAN production sub Sep 2026); SOCOM follow-on ($86M, 2025) after earlier ~$1B CUAS vehicle (2022).
companies.evidence_prototype_to_production: MEDIUM-STRONG: Army moved NGC2 'from prototyping to delivery' with Anduril leading the data baseline (Jun 2026) though no production dollar value was published; TITAN moved to production (Anduril sub, $65M, Sep 2026); CEO says >2x developmental systems transitioned to production in 2025 (company claim).
companies.tech_stack_inference_from_jobs: INFERENCE from Anduril job postings (Greenhouse, 2025-2026): Rust and Go for backend and the Distributed Service Bus (DSB) mesh networking layer handling multi-path routing across tactical radios, SATCOM and wired links in DDIL conditions; Kubernetes, GitOps, Terraform/Helm for cloud-to-edge deployment of Lattice OS; distributed simulation on Kubernetes; NixOS on NVIDIA Jetson edge devices (public jetpack-nixos repo). Salary band $191k-$253k for senior distributed-networks roles.
companies.confidence_notes: Contract facts (NGC2 $99.6M OTA, $20B enterprise ceiling, $87M task order, $86M SOCOM, TITAN $65M) are HIGH from multiple Tier 3 outlets quoting Army releases. Ceilings are explicitly NOT revenue; obligations under the $20B vehicle are unknown beyond the first task order. Headcount, cumulative funding and the NATO air-C2 selection are LOW-MEDIUM. Company performance claims from exercises (kill counts, timelines) are unverified. Primary sources (army.mil, anduril.com, developer.anduril.com, sbir.gov) were egress-blocked in this session; GitHub and PyPI were reachable.

c4isr_products.name: PANDA (Predictive Analytics and Decision Assistant) on C3 Agentic AI Platform / C3 AI Readiness
c4isr_products.description: USAF Rapid Sustainment Office system of record for CBM+/predictive maintenance monitoring hundreds of aircraft (B-1B, C-5, KC-135, KC-46, C-17, C-130J); production OTA ceiling raised from $100M (fully used over 5 years) to $450M through Oct 2029 (May 2025); first task order $13M (Jun 2025). C3 claims it 'may be the largest production AI deployment in the DoD'.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: flight, maintenance and supply data. Process: sensor-based ML algorithms, near-real-time analytics and data fusion. Output: predicted component failures, availability forecasts, maintenance recommendations. Users: USAF maintainers and logistics planners.

c4isr_products.name: C3 AI Decision Advantage (intelligence collection management) - Army PM Intelligence Systems & Analytics
c4isr_products.description: $23M award (Dec 2024, with ECS) to unify data from multiple systems to streamline ISR tasking and collection, digitizing scheduling workflows for real-time, predictive intelligence.
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: collection requirements, sensor availability, schedules. Process: optimization and workflow automation. Output: collection plans and tasking recommendations. Users: Army collection managers (G2/S2).

c4isr_products.name: Contested logistics application for Army RCCTO (HMI Formation platforms)
c4isr_products.description: Agentic/generative AI app predicting part shortages, fuel consumption and ammunition requirements for frontline vehicles in contested environments (announced Sep 2025).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: vehicle/formation logistics data. Process: forecasting agents. Output: real-time sustainment forecasts. Users: Army formation sustainers.

c4isr_products.name: C3 Generative AI for Intelligence Community / C3 AI Defense & Intelligence applications
c4isr_products.description: Intelligence analysis and document workflows for IC customers; NCIA, Royal Navy, RAF, Thales, BAE Systems, MDA, NAVAIR, NAVSEA, USMC named as customers in FY2025-FY2026 releases (values undisclosed).
c4isr_products.input_process_output_user: Input: unstructured intelligence and enterprise data. Process: retrieval and generative summarization. Output: analyst products. Users: IC analysts, allied defence staffs.
